html: The Iquito, who call themselves Ikitu, are a Zaparoan-speaking people of the Nanay River basin in Loreto, Peru, near the city of Iquitos, which takes its name from them. Jesuit missionaries gathered them into missions in the 1700s, and the rubber boom around 1900 and disease reduced them sharply. Their language is nearly extinct, with only a few elderly speakers, and since the 2000s linguists and community members have worked to record and teach it. Related languages include Arabela and Sápara.
